## Teaching points

1. Dipstick heme with few red cells suggests myoglobin. Track creatinine, potassium, urine output and compartment findings.
2. Use goal-directed fluids with repeat examination and urine-output assessment; avoid unmonitored fluid loading.
3. CK may remain high or continue rising after initial treatment. Improved perfusion does not prove muscle injury or electrolyte risk has resolved.
